doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Re-establishing himself in New York after Hampton
summary: Returning to the city was not hard; club owners care about the cash register.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So when you got off the Hampton band, then you sort of had to re-establish your reputation.

Back in the City, yeah. Well that wasn’t too hard to do you know, because club owners are funny. All they’re interested in is seeing the cash register ring. As long as the cash register keeps on ringing, most of them, they just go on about their business doing whatever they’re going to do. Some of them are musicians themselves. They just go on. Now if you kind of slack down and you ain’t doing the job now they’ll let you know, let you know quick.
